mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is negatively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns; higher rates compress equity valuations through increased discount rates, leading to negative 20-day returns when FEDFUNDS is high.
failure_condition: The rank IC of FEDFUNDS against 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation is not negative (p>0.05) in a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 experiences negative 5-day returns due to immediate market reactions to restrictive monetary policy.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the 5-day returns are positive, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) forms a monetary policy signal; when both are above their 50th percentiles, the S&P 500 experiences negative 60-day returns due to combined pressure from restrictive policy and high inflation.
failure_condition: The rank IC of the interaction signal (FEDFUNDS>4.5% and CPIAUCSL>200) against 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or in more than 40% of instances returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative 20-day returns due to expectations of prolonged economic weakness and potential rate cuts.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0%, the 20-day returns are positive, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The unemployment rate (UNRATE) is negatively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns; higher unemployment indicates economic weakness, leading to negative 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The rank IC of UNRATE against 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation is not negative (p>0.05) in a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 5.0%, the S&P 500 experiences positive 5-day returns due to improved economic sentiment and reduced risk of recession.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of instances where UNRATE < 5.0%, the 5-day returns are negative, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) forms a signal of economic expansion; when both are above their 50th percentiles, the S&P 500 experiences positive 60-day returns due to sustained economic growth.
failure_condition: The rank IC of the interaction signal (INDPRO>105 and HOUST>2200) against 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or in more than 40% of instances returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 200), the S&P 500 experiences negative 20-day returns due to central bank tightening and reduced real returns on equities.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 200, the 20-day returns are positive, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.
